top_story: Scrutiny of Israel’s conduct in the West Bank sharpened on 24 November as the army investigated allegations that soldiers used Palestinians as human shields, while Amnesty pressed the UK to deny space to an Israeli group promoting settlement in the same occupied territory. By 25 November, that pressure was undercut by Israeli minister Amichai Eliyahu’s parliamentary slurs against Palestinians and Muslims, which reinforced a climate of official dehumanisation that weakens restraints on abuse and deepens insecurity for Palestinian communities inside Israel and under occupation. In Yemen’s Hodeidah, renewed fighting, rising fuel costs, and collapsing household income pushed families closer to destitution, underscoring a regional pattern in which conflict and inflammatory politics translate directly into civilian precarity. The clearest takeaway is that abusive rhetoric and entrenched occupation are not separate from humanitarian decline; they help sustain the conditions that make it worse.
